approvedDesignText:
Add repeatable `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`, and add command help showing repeated selection, for example:

`gh project item-list 1 --owner "@me" --field Status --field Priority`

The two selection forms are mutually exclusive: any invocation containing both fails with a clear flag-validation error before project lookup. Field selection also conflicts with every explicit export/output modifier: `--format`, `--jq`/`-q`, and `--template`/`-t`. When a selection flag and any of those flags are supplied together, item-list returns a clear conflict error before field resolution or formatted/export output, including when the export modifier itself would otherwise be invalid alone.

Each repeated occurrence produces a separate added table column, in supplied order. Selected columns follow the existing `ID` column and use the project field’s canonical name as their headers. All requested fields are resolved before rendering. `--field` uses case-insensitive exact name matching; no match returns an actionable deterministic list of available names. Multiple matches return an actionable ambiguity error naming the requested field and listing candidate IDs in deterministic sorted order, directing the user to `--field-id`. `--field-id` matches case-sensitively; no match returns an actionable deterministic list of available `name (id)` choices.

The normal item-list request supplies the first page of project field definitions. When field selection is requested and that definition connection indicates further pages, fetch and append only the remaining pages using its returned cursor, then resolve against the complete definition list. Do not paginate field definitions when no selection flag is present. A field-definition pagination failure or any selection-resolution failure is returned as a useful error before table construction/rendering begins; therefore no partial table output is emitted. A project whose definitions fit in the normal response requires no extra field lookup/preflight request, while selections remain correct for projects with more field-definition pages.

For every item and selected field ID, find the corresponding returned field value; absent/unset values render as empty cells. Convert values to human-readable text: dates, text, and single-select values directly; iterations and milestones by title; numbers with compact decimal formatting and no forced trailing zeroes; labels as their names joined with `, `; pull requests as their URLs joined with `, `; users as their logins joined with `, `; reviewers as user logins and team names joined together with `, `; and repositories by URL. Before table output, normalize every selected value by removing carriage returns and replacing newlines with spaces, including every member of a multi-value field. Unknown returned value types render empty rather than misleading data.

Existing default table columns, query support, JSON/export behavior without selection, empty-project errors, and invocations without either new flag remain unchanged. Add parsing and help tests, tests for mutual exclusions against every output modifier, table/output and field-type rendering tests, diagnostics tests for deterministic ambiguity IDs, pagination/request tests, no-partial-output failure tests, and focused plus broader Go test execution.
